fields.place: South India, on the Kṛṣṇa-veṇṇā; Vṛndāvana (near Brahma-kuṇḍa; samādhi in Gopīnātha Bāzār)
fields.guru: Somagiri (dīkṣā, Gopāla-mantra); Cintāmaṇi, who showed him the way; Kṛṣṇa Himself (śikṣā); of Viṣṇusvāmī's line (Vallabha-digvijaya)
fields.notes: Līlāśuka, the author of the Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta, which Mahāprabhu found in South India and relished day and night (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 9.307-308). Saved from lust by the harlot Cintāmaṇi, initiated by Somagiri, he blinded himself and lived in Vṛndāvana, where Kṛṣṇa came to him as a cowherd boy. The Vallabha-digvijaya makes him the chief disciple of Viṣṇusvāmī. The record «Bilvamaṅgala» #1688 was joined to this one (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Advaita dāsa Bābājī (Vṛndāvana, kīrtanīyā)
fields.aka: Advaita Dāsa Bābājī Mahāśaya (Śrī Vṛndāvan), Advaita dāsa Paṇḍita, Bhīmakiśora Rakṣita (birth name)
fields.place: Born at Cāḍiyā (Sirajganj, Pabna); Murshidabad; Rādhākuṇḍa; Śāntipura; Navadvīpa; Vṛndāvana («Kāṅgālera Mahāprabhu»)
fields.guru: A descendant of Śrī Advaita (dīkṣā); Jagadānanda dāsa Paṇḍita of Rādhākuṇḍa (grammar); Gopīdāsa and Kṛṣṇadayāla Candra (kīrtana); Padmalocana Nāg Mahāśaya, whom he honoured as guru
fields.disciples: Nīlamaṇi Prabhu; kīrtanīyās who learned from him: Navadvīpa Vrajavāsī, Rai Bahadur Dhagendranāth Mitra, Gadādhara dāsa Bābājī, Bhakticaraṇa dāsa Bābājī
fields.notes: Born Bhīmakiśora Rakṣita, a Vārendra Kāyastha of Cāḍiyā; brought up by Padmalocana Nāg. Took veśa at 27, studied the Hari-nāmāmṛta-vyākaraṇa with Jagadānanda dāsa Paṇḍita of Rādhākuṇḍa, and became the last great master of the Garāṇhāṭī kīrtana. Grandfather of Bimanbihari Majumdar.

fields.aka: Lalitāsakhī Mātā, Lalitā dāsī, Jaygopāla, Gopāla Kṛṣṇa (birth name)
fields.place: Born at Hariseṇa (Gauranadi, Barisal); Calcutta; Hardwar; Navadvīpa (Rādhāramaṇa Bāg); Purī
fields.guru: Rādhāramaṇa-caraṇa dāsa Deva («Bābājī Mahāśaya»); blessed by his companion Caitanya dāsa
fields.works: Padas on Jhūlana, Rāsa and Holi; published the Carita-sudhā, the Śrī Surata-kathāmṛta and a Bengali Saṅgīta-mādhava
fields.notes:
Born Gopāla Kṛṣṇa, son of Kālīkānta Bhaṭṭācārya and Gaurasundarī of Hariseṇa. Met Rādhāramaṇa-caraṇa dāsa at Purī station in 1898 (called «Jaygopāla»); absorbed in the bhāva of Lalitā, named «Lalitā dāsī» by him; lived at Rādhāramaṇa Bāg, Navadvīpa, and published his guru's Carita-sudhā. Died 1946.

The record also held five short entries (Lalit Ghoṣāl, Lalit Sakhī, Lāl Puruṣottama, Locana dāsa, Locanānanda Gosvāmī), now in their own records (07-11-2026).

fields.name: Locanānanda Gosvāmī (with Navakiśora)
fields.guru: Navakiśora Gosvāmī (dīkṣā); Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābā of Govardhana (who taught them bhajana)
fields.notes: Of the line of a disciple of Nityānanda (Lakṣmīkānta Gosvāmī's family): Navakiśora, disciple of his elder brother Kṛṣṇakiśora, was his guru and inseparable friend. Both scholars of the six darśanas, they came to Vṛndāvana posing as low-caste Hāḍis and served Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābā of Govardhana, who taught them bhajana; back in East Bengal they installed Deities and preached; at the Ratha-yātrā in Purī, during the Pāṇḍu-vijaya, Navakiśora left his body and Locanānanda followed him at once; their samādhi is by Narendra-sarovara. (From the record of Lalitāsakhī dāsī, 07-11-2026.)
